task.title: Look at the sources of a fact
task.shortdesc: See which books and records back up a birth, a death or another fact, add a source to it, and say how reliable it is.

context.p: Each fact on a person's page has a small chip that counts its sources. A chip that says Sources: 0 means nothing backs that fact up yet. Every count of sources uses the same words, so you see them on a person's card in the results of a search too.

step.cmd: On the page of a person, choose the chip beside the fact, such as or .

stepresult.p: A sheet named opens. A fact with no source says No sources for this fact yet.
A box to search for a source you have already added opens. Use it when one book backs up many facts. The other choice is .
A sheet named opens. Under it lists the sources already in the tree. Choose one of them when one book backs up many facts.
A form opens. Only is needed. The other boxes hold the words copied from the record, a note, and where the source is kept. adds the author and the publisher.
The source is already attached to the fact. The sheet shows its title, and the buttons , , and .
The source is not attached yet. The next step opens. Its heading says Add, then the title of the source, then to this fact.

step.cmd: Choose , then fillFill in the page and how reliable the source is.

info.p: A citation says where in the source you found the fact. Enter the page, folio or entry in . Choose how good the evidence is in . If the entry has a date, enter it in .

cmd.ph: Choose at the bottom of the step.

stepresult.p: The sheet shows the title, the page and a line that starts Quality. The chip on the person's page shows the new count.
The step named opens. Its buttons, a camera, a folder and a chain, attach a photo, a file or a link to a copy of the record. You can leave it empty.

The sheet shows the title, the author and the page, and the buttons , , and . If you chose how reliable the source is, a line that starts Quality shows too. The chip on the person's page shows the new count.

result.p: The choices for how reliable a source is start with Not stated. They run from unreliable or worked out up to direct and primary evidence. They rate how good the evidence is. They do not say that the fact is true. A copy of a record, such as a transcription, is second-hand evidence.
A fact can have many sources. In the sample tree, the birth of Charlotte Brontë has five books, each with its author and a line for its quality.

When a fact has one place, such as a birth place or a death place, shows on the sheet. It opens a page that lists what each source says about the place and how good each source is. Use it when two records give different answers.
